Security Assumption: App images are scanned for vulnerabilities
Treatment Description: Perform vulnerability scanning on container images to identify and address security issues

Security Assumption: App uses minimal base images
Treatment Description: Use minimal base images to reduce attack surface and container footprint

Security Assumption: App images are signed and verified
Treatment Description: Sign and verify container images to ensure authenticity and integrity

Security Assumption: Dockerfiles of the app pin the base image version
Treatment Description: Pin base image versions in Dockerfiles to ensure reproducibility and control updates

Security Assumption: App images are rebuilt and updated regularly
Treatment Description: Rebuild and update container images regularly to address vulnerabilities and apply patches

Security Assumption: Device orchestration only uses trusted image registries
Treatment Description: Use only trusted and verified image registries for container deployment

Security Assumption: App containers are run as non-root user
Treatment Description: Configure containers to run with non-root user privileges to limit potential damage

Security Assumption: App containers use read-only file systems
Treatment Description: Mount container filesystem as read-only to prevent malicious file modifications

Security Assumption: App containers are deployed with minimal Linux capabilities
Treatment Description: Deploy containers with minimal Linux capabilities to reduce attack surface

Security Assumption: Seccomp is implemented on the device
Treatment Description: Implement Seccomp profiles to restrict system calls available to containers

Security Assumption: AppArmor is implemented on the device
Treatment Description: Implement AppArmor profiles to enforce mandatory access control for containers

Security Assumption: SELinux is implemented on the device
Treatment Description: Implement SELinux policies to provide mandatory access control for containers

Security Assumption: App containers have minimal access to host resources
Treatment Description: Minimize container access to host resources through proper isolation and restrictions

Security Assumption: Authentication for exposed container APIs is enforced
Treatment Description: Enforce authentication mechanisms for all exposed container APIs

Security Assumption: Role-based access control is used for orchestration and container management
Treatment Description: Implement role-based access control for container orchestration and management

Security Assumption: Access to container management interfaces (e.g., Docker socket) is restricted
Treatment Description: Restrict access to container management interfaces to authorized users and processes

Security Assumption: App container networks are segmented
Treatment Description: Implement network segmentation to limit container communication and reduce attack spread

Security Assumption: Host-level firewall rules and network policies are applied
Treatment Description: Configure host-level firewall rules and network policies to control traffic

Security Assumption: Inter-container communication is encrypted
Treatment Description: Encrypt inter-container communication to protect data in transit

Security Assumption: Ingress/egress controls for containers are implemented
Treatment Description: Implement ingress and egress controls to restrict container network traffic

Security Assumption: Secure secrets management tools (e.g. vaults or secrets manager) are used
Treatment Description: Use secure secrets management tools for credential storage and handling

Security Assumption: Apps do not contain any hardcoded secrets
Treatment Description: Prohibit hardcoded secrets in application code and container images

Security Assumption: Secrets at rest and in transit are encrypted
Treatment Description: Encrypt secrets both at rest and in transit to protect sensitive data

Security Assumption: Automatic secret rotation and revocation policies are implemented
Treatment Description: Implement automatic secret rotation and revocation policies for credentials

Security Assumption: The container runtime on the host device is up to date
Treatment Description: Keep container runtime on host devices up to date with security patches

Security Assumption: The host device is deployed as an immutable infrastructure (e.g. read-only file system)
Treatment Description: Deploy host devices as immutable infrastructure to prevent unauthorized modifications

Security Assumption: The host device is monitored for unauthorized changes
Treatment Description: Monitor host devices for unauthorized changes and configuration drift

Security Assumption: Container-level logging is enabled
Treatment Description: Enable comprehensive container-level logging for security monitoring and audit

Security Assumption: Processes on the host device are monitored for anomalous behavior
Treatment Description: Monitor host processes for anomalous behavior and suspicious activities

Security Assumption: Runtime security tools (e.g. Falco, Trivy) are used
Treatment Description: Deploy runtime security tools to detect and respond to container threats

Security Assumption: Incident response procedures are implemented
Treatment Description: Implement and maintain incident response procedures for container security events

Security Assumption: Logs are centralized and protected
Treatment Description: Centralize logs and implement protection mechanisms to ensure integrity

Security Assumption: Decoy containers (honeypots) are deployed on the device to detect malicious activity
Treatment Description: Deploy decoy containers as honeypots to detect malicious activities

Security Assumption: Container API calls and orchestration events are monitored for anomalies
Treatment Description: Monitor container API calls and orchestration events for anomalous patterns

Security Assumption: Alerts are triggered for unauthorized access attempts to container registries or APIs
Treatment Description: Configure alerts for unauthorized access attempts to registries and APIs

Security Assumption: The CI/CD pipeline for the app is secured (regarding code repositories, build environments, secrets, vulnerabilities, signing, auditing ...)
Treatment Description: Secure CI/CD pipeline to prevent supply chain attacks and ensure build integrity

Security Assumption: SBOMs are used for the app to track code dependencies
Treatment Description: Use Software Bill of Materials to track and manage application dependencies

Security Assumption: Code reviews and automated testing of the app are enforced
Treatment Description: Enforce code reviews and automated testing to identify security issues early

Security Assumption: Third-party components used by the app are validated
Treatment Description: Validate third-party components for security vulnerabilities and trustworthiness

Security Assumption: The CI/CD pipeline for the app enables reproducible builds
Treatment Description: Enable reproducible builds in CI/CD pipeline to ensure build consistency

Security Assumption: Apps for development and production are not deployed in the same environment
Treatment Description: Separate development and production environments to reduce security risks

Security Assumption: Regular risk assessments of apps and host devices are performed
Treatment Description: Perform regular risk assessments of applications and host infrastructure

Security Assumption: The operation's asset inventory is maintained
Treatment Description: Maintain comprehensive asset inventory for container infrastructure

Security Assumption: Container security policies along the app lifecycle are documented and enforced
Treatment Description: Document and enforce container security policies throughout application lifecycle

Security Assumption: Periodic audits and reviews of apps and host devices are conducted
Treatment Description: Conduct periodic security audits and reviews of containers and host devices
